text: This equips K⊗ₖH with its scalar-extended Hopf structure over K. The tensor product identifies coefficients through the specified ring map k→K, as in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3); it need not embed H. The construction works for arbitrary commutative base rings and introduces neither flatness nor finite-generation assumptions. Checks pass: [baseChangeMap_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L98), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L241).
Scalar-extended coordinate maps act on the H factor.
Its points extend by the tensor formula s⊗h↦s·f(h).

A coordinate morphism φ:H→L extends to id_K⊗φ, sending s⊗h to s⊗φ(h). The tensor construction preserves the coproduct and counit, hence also the antipode between Hopf algebras. This is functorial scalar extension as in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), with no injectivity or flatness requirement on k→K. Checks pass: [hom_baseChangeMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L89), [baseChangeMap_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L98).
The underlying bialgebra map is the stated tensor map.
The concrete action changes only the H factor.

Forgetting the categorical wrapper leaves exactly the bialgebra map id_K⊗φ. Thus the selected morphism carries the usual tensor-product operation in [Stacks, tensor products](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). The inspected source additionally proves coalgebra compatibility; this identifies the stored structure as well as the function. No injectivity of either tensor-factor map is assumed in identifying the underlying morphism. Checks pass: [baseChangeMap_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L98), [baseChangeFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L184).
Evaluation gives the defining pure-tensor formula.
The functor uses precisely this scalar-extended morphism.

The extended coordinate map sends a pure tensor s⊗h to s⊗φ(h), leaving the new scalar unchanged. Bilinearity makes this prescription well defined on the tensor-product relations and determines the entire map, as in [Stacks, tensor products](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). It does not assert that every tensor is pure or that h↦1⊗h is injective. Checks pass: [hom_baseChangeMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L89), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeMap_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L434).
The map is the tensor product with the identity.
The same formula computes transported GL coordinate morphisms.

A surjective coordinate map remains surjective after any scalar extension: pure tensors have preimages, and their finite sums generate the tensor product. This is the right-exactness statement in [Stacks, tensor products](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). Flatness is unnecessary here; the conclusion concerns surjectivity of coordinate algebras, whose corresponding affine-scheme arrows run in the opposite direction. Checks pass: [baseChangeMap_surjective_of_iso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L382), [mem_baseChangeHopfIdeal_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L119).
Surjectivity is retained after changing source and target presentations.
The scalar-extended quotient map defines the native base-changed Hopf ideal.

An injective coordinate map remains injective after tensoring with K provided K is flat over k. This is exactly the injection-preserving property in [Stacks, flatness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9), applied to the underlying linear map. The bracketed flatness hypothesis is essential to this general argument; mere injectivity of the ring map k→K is not substituted for it. Checks pass: [baseChangeMap_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L98), [faithfullyFlat_iff_injective_of_isGeometricallyReduced](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeometricallyReduced/FaithfullyFlat.lean#L42).
The map being tested is id_K⊗φ.
An actual field-extension consumer uses this injection preservation before applying its own stronger geometric hypotheses.

Scalar extension sends H to K⊗ₖH and each coordinate morphism to id_K⊗φ. The source proves identity and composition by checking pure tensors, matching functoriality in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). These arrows remain coordinate-algebra arrows; passing to affine schemes reverses them. The construction does not assert that scalar extension reflects morphism equality. Checks pass: [baseChangeFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L178), [baseChangeFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L184).
The object assignment is the specified tensor-product Hopf algebra.
The morphism assignment is the specified tensor map.

For compatible ring maps k→E→K, this identifies K⊗ᴱ(E⊗ₖH) with K⊗ₖH by s⊗(e⊗h)↦(e·s)⊗h. Its inverse inserts 1 in the E factor. This is associativity of scalar extension from [Stacks, tensor products](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV), with the coproduct and counit also preserved. Compatibility of the three scalar actions is explicitly assumed. Checks pass: [baseChangeTowerIso_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L206), [baseChangeTowerIso_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L212).
The forward map absorbs the intermediate scalar.
The inverse inserts the intermediate unit.

A K-algebra point of K⊗ₖH corresponds to a k-algebra point of H in the same value ring, with scalars restricted. Restriction evaluates at 1⊗h; extension sends s⊗h to s·f(h). The tensor adjunction in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3) supplies these inverse maps, and the inspected proof additionally verifies compatibility with convolution multiplication. Checks pass: [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L232), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L241), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_mapValue](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L256).
Restriction evaluates the original point at 1⊗h.
Extension multiplies its value by the new scalar.
The equivalence commutes with change of value algebra.

The points equivalence restricts a K-algebra map by h↦1⊗h, so its value is exactly f(1⊗h). The value ring itself is unchanged; only its scalar structure is restricted to k. This is the restriction formula in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), used here for convolution groups without requiring the structural map H→K⊗ₖH to be injective. Checks pass: [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L241), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_mapDomain](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L281).
The inverse has the matching extension formula.
Restriction is compatible with coordinate morphisms.

Scalar extension identifies K⊗ᴿR[Xᵢⱼ,det(X)⁻¹] with K[Xᵢⱼ,det(X)⁻¹]. The construction commutes tensor product with polynomial rings and determinant localization, preserving the coordinate presentation of [Milne, IV §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). It works for every commutative ring map R→K, including nonflat maps; rank zero uses the empty determinant 1 and gives the base ring. Checks pass: [coordinateRingBaseChangeAlgEquiv_tmul_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L111), [coordinateRingBaseChangeAlgEquiv_symm_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L131).
Polynomial coordinates extend coefficients and multiply by the new scalar.
The inverse recovers their unit pure tensors.

A scalar tensored with a polynomial coordinate becomes that scalar times the polynomial with coefficients mapped from R to K. This characterizes the usual change of coefficients in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3) after determinant localization. The scalar action is ordinary multiplication through K’s structural map, and no injectivity of the coefficient map is needed. Checks pass: [coordinateRingBaseChangeAlgEquiv_one_tmul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L123), [coordinateRingBaseChangeAlgEquiv_symm_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L131).
Individual matrix coordinates retain their indices.
The inverse recovers the original polynomial coordinate tensor.

Two K-algebra maps from the scalar-extended GL coordinate algebra agree if they agree on 1⊗xᵢⱼ. Scalars are already fixed by K-linearity, and the image of the inverted determinant is forced by uniqueness of inverses, as in [Stacks, localization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CM). Thus a separate determinant-inverse generator check is unnecessary, even over rings with zero divisors. Checks pass: [coordinateRingBaseChangeAlgEquiv_one_tmul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L123), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeBialgEquiv_one_tmul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L264).
The canonical comparison has these prescribed generator values.
The same values hold for the stored Hopf structures.

The coordinate-ring base-change equivalence also preserves coproduct and counit, checked on generic matrix entries using the formulas of [Milne, IV §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). It therefore identifies the chosen Hopf structures, since a bialgebra map between Hopf algebras preserves antipodes automatically. No flatness, field or positive-rank assumption is added to the commutative-ring hypotheses. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeBialgEquiv_one_tmul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L264), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeBialgEquiv_one_tmul_localizedGenericMatrix_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L281).
The equivalence preserves generic matrix entries.
It also preserves actual inverse-matrix entries.

The Hopf comparison sends s⊗p(X) to s times p(X) with coefficients extended to K, exactly as its underlying coordinate-ring comparison. Thus bundling the coproduct and counit does not change the polynomial action in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The coordinate-ring-to-Hopf equivalences only identify the chosen presentations; they introduce no alternative coordinate substitutions. Checks pass: [coordinateRingBaseChangeAlgEquiv_tmul_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L111), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeBialgEquiv_symm_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L244).
The underlying algebra comparison has the same formula.
The inverse recovers the unit tensor of each extended polynomial.

The inverse Hopf comparison sends a polynomial with coefficients extended from R back to 1⊗p(X). Applying the forward equivalence proves the formula, matching coefficient extension in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). This concerns polynomials in the image of R’s coefficient map; it does not assume every polynomial over K has all coefficients in that image. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeBialgEquiv_tmul_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L232), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_inv_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L416).
The forward formula verifies the inverse value.
The categorical inverse has the corresponding matrix-generator formula.

This packages the explicit GL Hopf equivalence as a categorical isomorphism, retaining the coordinate presentation of [Milne, IV §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). Both directions are actual inverse Hopf morphisms. The displayed universe condition concerns how the bundled carriers fit into one category, not a restriction on ring elements; no flatness or injectivity of R→K is assumed. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom_one_tmul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L340), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_inv_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L416).
The forward morphism preserves generic entries.
The inverse returns their unit pure tensors.

The categorical isomorphism sends s⊗p(X) to s times the coefficient-extended polynomial coordinate. This proves that the categorical packaging has the intended concrete action, rather than merely providing some abstract isomorphism of GL coordinate rings. It agrees with the change-of-coefficients presentation in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), for arbitrary commutative coefficient rings. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeBialgEquiv_tmul_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L232), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L396).
The underlying bialgebra equivalence has this formula.
The inverse reconstructs the scalar pure tensor.

The forward comparison sends 1⊗xᵢⱼ to the generic matrix entry xᵢⱼ over K, with the same row and column indices. This fixes the matrix-coordinate convention of [Milne, IV §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51); there is no transpose or index reversal hidden in the bundled isomorphism. If n=0 there are no entry indices, consistently with the empty matrix. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L325), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_inv_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L416).
The formula specializes the polynomial-coordinate equation.
The inverse returns the original entry tensor.

The comparison carries 1⊗det(X) to det(X) over K because determinant is a polynomial in the entries and ring maps preserve it. This is the determinant character in [Milne, IV §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), expressed as a group-like coordinate element, not an algebra-valued point. At rank zero both determinants are 1, so the statement remains valid. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L325), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom_genericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L372).
The general polynomial formula applies to the determinant polynomial.
The whole generic matrix is preserved entrywise.

Applying scalar extension and the comparison to every generic matrix entry gives the generic matrix over K. The coefficient map is explicitly restricted to R so the composite has the required scalar structure. This is the matrix-level form of the GL presentation in [Milne, IV §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), with neither a transpose nor a change of basis. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom_one_tmul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L340), [pointToGeneralLinear_baseChangeMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L490).
Each matrix entry satisfies the asserted formula.
Actual points read the same invertible matrix after this transport.

The inverse comparison sends an extended polynomial coordinate to 1⊗p(X); multiplying by s gives s⊗p(X). Here the dot denotes the K-scalar action, which moves to the first tensor factor by bilinearity, as in [Stacks, tensor products](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). No division by s or assumption that s is a unit occurs in the formula. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeBialgEquiv_symm_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L244), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L325).
The underlying inverse gives the unit tensor.
The forward comparison restores the scalar polynomial value.

The inverse categorical comparison takes a generic entry over K to 1⊗xᵢⱼ over R. This is the generator-level inverse to coefficient extension in [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), with unchanged matrix indices. It is the inverse of the Hopf-algebra comparison, not the inverse matrix operation supplied separately by the antipode. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L396), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom_one_tmul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L340).
This specializes the inverse polynomial formula at scalar one.
The forward comparison returns the same generic entry.

To transport a coordinate morphism after base change, first use the inverse GL comparison, then tensor the morphism, then apply the chosen target isomorphism. On xᵢⱼ the result is therefore e(1⊗f(xᵢⱼ)). This makes the natural scalar-extension construction of [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3) explicit; categorical composition follows that written order. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_inv_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L416), [baseChangeMap_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean#L98), [pointToGeneralLinear_baseChangeMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L490).
The initial transport sends the entry to its unit tensor.
The middle map applies the original coordinate morphism.
Evaluation confirms the associated matrix is unchanged.

The same canonical GL Hopf isomorphism lifts to the category of finitely generated coordinate algebras. Scalar extension preserves finite type by [Stacks, base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3); the extra category records this property without changing the morphisms. Finite type here means finitely generated as an algebra, not finite-dimensional as a module or a finite set of points. Checks pass: [finiteTypeCoordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L524), [coordinateHopfAlgebraBaseChangeIso_hom_one_tmul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L340).
Forgetting finite type recovers the concrete Hopf comparison.
Its underlying morphism preserves the generic matrix entries.

ENorm supplies only a function with values in the nonnegative reals together with infinity. The notation does not by itself assert a triangle inequality, continuity, or that only zero has norm zero. Indeed, the underlying type need not even have addition or a distinguished zero element. Compared with [Faris §§16.2,16.11](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L74).

A continuous extended norm is an extended nonnegative-valued function continuous for the given topology and the usual order topology on its values. No additive laws or separation condition are included. In particular, the topology on the domain need not be determined by the norm, and infinite values remain allowed. Compared with [Faris §16.8](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L111).

This structure gives an additive monoid a continuous extended norm that vanishes at zero and satisfies the triangle inequality. Other elements may also have norm zero, and infinite values are allowed. Addition need not commute, and neither additive inverses nor scalar homogeneity nor continuity of addition are required. Compared with [Faris §§16.2,23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L117).

This is the commutative additive version: a continuous extended norm vanishes at zero and is subadditive, while addition commutes. Nonzero elements can still have norm zero, and no additive inverses or scalar action are needed. The domain topology is supplied independently; it need not arise from an extended metric. Compared with [Faris §23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L155).

An extended normed additive monoid adds the condition that norm zero occurs exactly at the additive identity. The norm is continuous and subadditive, but can take the value infinity. No inverse operation, scalar multiplication, or metric topology is required, so this is broader than a normed vector space. Compared with [Faris §§16.2,23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L128).

This combines commutative addition with a continuous, subadditive extended norm that is zero exactly at the additive identity. Values may be infinite, and the given topology need not be a metric topology. The nonnegative extended real numbers, with their order topology and norm equal to the value itself, are an intended example. Compared with [Faris §§16.11,23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L167).

A normed additive group has a finite real norm inducing a genuine metric by d(x,y)=‖−x+y‖. The operation need not commute: this convention makes left translations preserve distance. Zero norm forces the element to be zero, but neither a vector-space scalar action nor completeness is part of the structure. Compared with [Cornulier–de la Harpe §4.B](https://www.normalesup.org/~cornulier/MetricLC.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L207).

Every normed abelian group can also be treated as a seminormed abelian group by retaining its operation, norm, and distance. The weaker interface no longer requires separation, but this conversion does not identify elements or change any distances. The original group still has zero norm only at zero. Compared with [Faris §23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L276).

A seminormed abelian group supplies the structure of a general seminormed additive group using the same operation and norm. Commutativity becomes unnecessary for results using the weaker interface; it is not destroyed. Distinct elements may have zero distance, and this conversion introduces no quotient, new metric, or scalar action. Compared with [Cornulier–de la Harpe §4.B](https://www.normalesup.org/~cornulier/MetricLC.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L282).

A normed abelian group is also a normed additive group with the same norm, operation, and metric. This conversion permits results that do not need commutativity while retaining separation by distance zero. It does not construct a different group, weaken the metric to a pseudometric, or introduce scalar multiplication. Compared with [Cornulier–de la Harpe §4.B](https://www.normalesup.org/~cornulier/MetricLC.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Defs.lean#L288).

The chosen real norm is absolute value. It returns x for nonnegative x and −x for nonpositive x, so negative inputs have nonnegative norm rather than being truncated to zero. This declaration selects the function; the compatible additive-group and metric structure is supplied by the accompanying normed-group instance. Compared with [Faris §§16.2–16.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Real.lean#L54).

The real numbers form a normed abelian group under their usual addition, with norm |x| and distance |x−y|. The compatibility equation identifies the existing real metric with the norm of a difference. This instance packages additive and metric structure; it does not add or require scalar homogeneity or completeness. Compared with [Faris §§16.1–16.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Real.lean#L61).

The product of two normed abelian groups uses coordinatewise addition and the maximum of the two component norms. Thus the norm of a real pair (3,4) is 4 under this product convention. This is the sup norm, not an implicit choice of Euclidean norm, and no scalar field is needed. Compared with [Faris §16.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Constructions.lean#L286).

A finite family of normed abelian groups has the maximum norm on its product, with coordinatewise addition. The factors may differ. For an empty index set there is one empty function and its norm is zero, using the empty supremum of nonnegative norms. Finiteness is required; arbitrary infinite products are not covered. Compared with [Faris §16.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Constructions.lean#L461).

The extended norm of a nonnegative extended real number is the number itself. In particular, zero has norm zero and infinity has norm infinity. No conversion to an ordinary real number occurs, so infinity is not replaced by zero. This declaration supplies the function; its additive and continuity laws are separate. Compared with [Faris §16.11](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Real.lean#L39).

An element of a normed additive group has strictly positive norm exactly when it is nonzero. The norm is a real number, and separation is essential: a seminorm may vanish on nonzero elements. No commutativity, scalar field, or completeness assumption is needed for this equivalence. Compared with [Faris §16.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Basic.lean#L997).

The norm of a sum is at most the sum of the norms. This triangle inequality already holds for a seminormed additive group, so separation and a scalar field are unnecessary. The addition need not commute, and the inequality may be strict because cancellation can make the sum much smaller. Compared with [Faris §§16.2,23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Basic.lean#L102).

The norm of a finite sum is bounded by the sum of the individual norms. The index set has no repeated indices, but equal values at different indices still contribute separately. The empty sum gives 0≤0. Commutative addition makes the unordered sum meaningful; no convergence or completeness hypothesis is involved. Compared with [Faris §§16.2,23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Basic.lean#L799).

Adding an element to itself n times has norm at most n times its norm. Here n is a natural number, and the right-hand product is real multiplication after converting n to a real. Only an inequality is asserted: general group norms need not be homogeneous, and n=0 gives zero on both sides. Compared with [Faris §23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Basic.lean#L436).

Reversing a difference does not change its norm: ‖a−b‖=‖b−a‖. Subtraction here is the additive-group operation a+(−b), not truncated subtraction of natural numbers. The two differences are additive inverses, whose norms agree. This remains true for seminorms and does not require the group operation to commute. Compared with [Cornulier–de la Harpe §4.B](https://www.normalesup.org/~cornulier/MetricLC.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Basic.lean#L69).

For an abelian sheaf F on any topological space X and closed S, this sheafifies the local support-cohomology groups. These are Ext groups deriving sections that vanish outside S. The result is a sheaf on X supported on S; degree zero is the kernel of restriction to the complement, not the restriction of F to S. See [Grothendieck–Hartshorne, LNM41, Proposition 1.2, p.4](https://djvu.online/file/53c09w4w7AaBC) and [the definition and native comparisons](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Topology/Sheaves/LocalCohomology.lean#L236). [HF0](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4adc7e3d0b68a8bb9974126e7411667cb533255f/TauCetiRoadmap/Hyperfunctions/README.md#L97) specifies this construction; [Scheme §2.7 Checks](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4adc7e3d0b68a8bb9974126e7411667cb533255f/TauCetiRoadmap/SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md#L3519) concern global groups and module comparisons, so none are certified here. Native Checks pass: [stalks vanish off S](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Topology/Sheaves/LocalCohomology.lean#L258) and [positive degrees vanish for flasque F](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Topology/Sheaves/LocalCohomology.lean#L269).
Stalks of the local cohomology sheaf vanish outside the closed support.
For a flasque coefficient sheaf, local cohomology sheaves vanish in every positive degree.
